deep.reconstruction:
Context: Göttingen observatory, May 1819, meridian circle observations; the previous page carries the year 1819. Each star line has the form: wire transit times | circle reading (approximately the zenith distance) | microscope or micrometer readings. Below it come barometer in Paris inches and lines (27^2 4^l6 = 27 in 4.6 lines) and two thermometer readings.

(1) Clock correction from alpha Orionis, 7 May.
- Wire times: 5h44m58.5s, 5h45m14.9s, 5h45m31.4s.
- My filled step: mean = (58.5 + 74.9 + 91.4)/3 = 74.933 s, so T = 5h45m14.93s.
- Tabular apparent RA: 5h45m18.367s + 0.023s = 5h45m18.39s.
- Clock correction: dT = 18.39 - 14.93 = +3.46 s.
- Circle reading 44°12'49.2", microscopes 3'1.5" and 2'41.5". This agrees with the zenith distance 51°32' - 7°22' ≈ 44°10' plus the instrument's index.

(2) Clock correction from Sirius.
- Wire times: 46.7s, 6h37m3.2s, 20.2s.
- Mean = (46.7 + 63.2 + 80.2)/3 = 63.367 s, so T = 6h37m3.37s.
- Apparent RA: 6h37m6.799s + 0.001s = 6h37m6.80s.
- Clock correction: dT = +3.43 s, consistent with Orionis to 0.03 s.
- Circle reading 68°1'42.5" (zenith distance about 51°32' + 16°29'), microscopes 1'55.4" and 1'33.1".

(3) Level (Libelle), 7 May.
- Two rows of three readings: (3'18.7", 3'28.6", 3'11.9") and (3'18.7", 3'28.0", 3'10.9").
- Column means: 3'18.7", 3'28.3", 3'11.4".
- The marginal 0.53" is the mean of the row differences: (0 + 0.6 + 1.0)/3 = 0.533.

(4) Level, 8 May.
- Rows: (23.1, 32.7, 15.6) and (18.2, 27.2, 10.3).
- Column means: 20.65, 29.95, 12.95.
- Mean row difference: (4.9 + 5.5 + 5.3)/3 = 5.233, written 5.23".

(5) alpha Cassiopeiae and Polaris, 8 May.
- alpha Cas: transits 0h30m8.5s and 38.0s (first wire missing). Circle reading about -4°0' (north of zenith: 51°32' - 55°31' ≈ -4°), readings 3'33.0", 3'42.6", 3'24.6".
- Polaris: circle reading about 36°45', readings 1'9.9", 1'19.6", 1'1.8".
- Weather: barometer 27 in 5.4 lines, thermometers 12.4° and 14.2°.

(6) Latitude from Polaris.
- Polaris was observed on both horizontal wires, reading only the lower microscope. The individual wire reductions are on the next page.
- Mean observed zenith distance: z0 = 36°47'10.75".
- Refraction 41.61" is added: z = 36°47'52.36".
- With the apparent declination from the next page, delta = 88°20'8.02", for upper culmination north of the zenith: phi = delta - z = 88°20'8.02" - 36°47'52.36" = 51°32'15.66".
- This compares with 51°32'8.64" from the sun at noon on the previous page.

(7) Logarithmic refraction computation (my reconstruction).
- log 0.9806 ≈ 9.99150 and 9.99142 are the barometric and thermometric correction factors. Their sum is 9.98292 (factor 0.9614).
- The last number, read 9.63629, must be 1.63629 = log 43.28". That is the mean refraction at z ≈ 36°48', equal to 57.85"·tan z.
- Then 1.63629 + 9.98292 - 10 = 1.61921 = log 41.61", the refraction actually applied.
- These are routine reductions of meridian-circle observations for the clock error and the latitude of the Göttingen observatory.
errors: The final logarithm 9.63629 only makes sense as 1.63629 (log of the mean refraction 43.28"). Either Gauss wrote the characteristic loosely or the transcription misreads it; the mantissa is consistent.

The barometric/thermometric factors (9.99150, 9.99142) could not be independently reproduced exactly without knowing Gauss's refraction table and its normal pressure and temperature. They are consistent to about 1e-4 with 27 in 5.4 lines against a 28 in standard.

results.what: Clock correction from mean of three wire transits compared with apparent RA (alpha Ori +3.46s, Sirius +3.43s)
Level readings averaged; mean row difference as level inclination
Latitude of Göttingen observatory from Polaris upper culmination: phi = delta - z, with refraction computed logarithmically as mean refraction times barometer and thermometer factors
results.modern_name: Latitude determination from circumpolar star meridian zenith distance with refraction correction
results.usually_credited_to: standard practice; Gauss's Göttingen latitude work is well known

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine 1819 observational reductions (clock error, level, refraction, latitude) in Gauss's observatory journal. Gauss's astronomical observing at Göttingen is well documented.

checkable.asserts: mean of alpha Ori wire times = 14.933 s past 5h45m
mean of Sirius wire times = 3.367 s past 6h37m
